newsitem.title: USA: USDA says tightening up school lunch inspections.
newsitem.headline: USDA says tightening up school lunch inspections.

text.p: To prevent another outbreak of Hepatitis A in the U.S. school lunch program, the Agriculture Department said Thursday it would demand more information from food processors.

Earlier this month, U.S. health officials launched an investigation of a California strawberry processor after the fruit was blamed for causing some 179 cases of hepatitis among schoolchildren and teachers in Michigan.
The unit of Epitope Inc acknowledged that the berries came from Mexico in violation of USDA rules that require only domestic food can be sold to the U.S. school lunch program.

Mary Ann Keeffe, a USDA acting undersecretary, said the agency is requiring more information from sellers when they certify the domestic origin of their products. The documentation and "more detailed reviews" will be conducted before a product is shipped, she said.
The agency is also stepping up its practice of supplier audits after deliveries have been made, she said.
"To date, no additional reports of illness linked to frozen strawberries have been confirmed by the Center for Disease Control," Keeffe told a House Education subcommittee.
The USDA, the Food and Drug Administration and the U.S. Attorney in San Diego are conducting a criminal investigation to determine if Epitope should face criminal fraud charges, she said.
The strawberries were traced to five other states, Arizona, California, Georgia, Iowa and Tennessee in shipments that began last May, investigators said.
